Wagner Design Lab: How a Facade Becomes a Business Card

The Wagner Design Lab in Langenneufnach implements the corporate philosophy of design and movement architecturally – with large glass surfaces and Trespa facade panels. The XXL glasses measuring 3.04 x 19.21 m come from sedak.

Architects Titus Bernhard and Andreas Weißenbach designed a structure measuring 52 x 12 x 6 meters that rests on slender steel stilts and hovers above the existing building.

In Langenneufnach, Swabia, the Wagner Design Lab was created as a commercial building that expresses the corporate philosophy of the Wagner brand in its architecture. For the builders Peter and Rainer Wagner, who run the company Topstar, the preservation of the family home as the seed of the business was paramount, complemented by a new building aimed at the future. The project received the German Design Award even before its completion.

A “Showcase of Superlatives”

The glass surfaces symbolize insight and far-sightedness.

Architects Titus Bernhard and Andreas Weißenbach conceptualized a structure measuring 52 x 12 x 6 m, resting on slender steel stilts and hovering above the existing building, which they called a “showcase of superlatives.”

Four triple-glazed panels measuring 3.04 x 19.21 m and weighing seven tons each were installed. These glass surfaces symbolize insight and far-sightedness.

The Wagner Design Lab serves as an idea factory, creative space, and showroom for the office area. It aims to inspire creatives and visitors. The company focuses on the integration of design, movement, and space, which is reflected in dynamic sitting. This dynamics should also be visible in the architecture.

The building envelope reflects themes of dynamics and contrast. For this purpose, “Trespa Meteon” panels were used. The facade features polygons in the decor “Lumen Metropolis Black,” forming a geometric honeycomb structure. The undersides and interiors of the cantilevered roof and facade areas are in “Lumen Athens White,” contrasting with the recessed glass surfaces. The architects emphasize the dominant effect of the large glass surfaces in combination with the black polygonal Trespa elements.

Light plays an important role. Thanks to the large glass surfaces, it remains natural and finds its way from inside to outside through the light surfaces. This leads to a merging of architecture with nature. The selected “Lumen” decors from Trespa utilize natural light for facade design.

The surface “Diffuse” absorbs light evenly across the entire area. It is matte and smooth, free of gloss and patterns, which adds depth to the black and white and contributes to a calm appearance of the facade. The building integrates seamlessly and glare-free into its surroundings.

A minimalist approach demands precision.

Bernhard describes his design philosophy as “sensual minimalism,” a reduced form language, careful material selection, and craftsmanship details. The Wagner Design Lab illustrates this minimalism, demanding a high level of implementation. Bernhard emphasizes that minimalism forgives no mistakes, and everything must be thought out precisely.

The architects chose Trespa because it met the demands for precision, durability, and a cohesive design. The material is characterized by robustness and good processability. The installation was concealed using a manufacturer-certified system solution “TS200.” This employs clamps on an aluminum substructure and integrated adjusting screws. Thus, the panels can be aligned with millimeter precision both vertically and horizontally to achieve an exact joint pattern.

Weißenbach designed the facade with detailed planning and technical understanding, supported by Trespa.

# Rewindo: PVC-Altfenster-Recycling steigt auf 141.595 Tonnen

09.09.2026
\| [Druckvorschau](https://www.glaswelt.de/node/264508/print "Druckvorschau")

Rewindo verzeichnete 2025 einen Zuwachs von 32,3 Prozent bei den Recyclingmengen von PVC-Altfenstern und artverwandten Produkten. Die Recyclingquote erreichte 94,5 Prozent.

![Rewindo verzeichnete 2025 einen Zuwachs von 32,3 Prozent bei den Recyclingmengen von PVC-Altfenstern und artverwandten Produkten.](https://www.glaswelt.de/sites/default/files/styles/aurora_default/public/aurora/2026/09/561622.jpeg?itok=LZBK_QKo)

Rewindo

Rewindo verzeichnete 2025 einen Zuwachs von 32,3 Prozent bei den Recyclingmengen von PVC-Altfenstern und artverwandten Produkten.

Die Rewindo GmbH Fenster-Recycling-Service, Bonn, meldete für das Jahr 2025 eine deutliche Steigerung der Recyclingmenge. Mit einem Zuwachs von 32,3 Prozent wurde die höchste Wachstumsrate seit der Gründung des Unternehmens im Jahr 2002 erreicht. Insgesamt wurden 141.595 Tonnen PVC-Altfenster und zugehörige Produkte recycelt, nach 131.000 Tonnen im Vorjahr.

Im Bereich der Post-Consumer-Produkte wurden laut Recovinyl (Database RecoTraceTM) 58.358 Tonnen PVC-Altfenster, -Rollläden und artverwandte Produkte erfasst. Dies entspricht einer Zunahme gegenüber den 44.109 Tonnen des Jahres 2024. Zusätzlich fielen 83.237 Tonnen Produktions- und Verarbeitungsabfälle an. Das Unternehmen leistet damit einen Beitrag zur Erreichung der Recyclingziele von VinylPlus®, der Selbstverpflichtung der europäischen PVC-Branche.

## Recyclingquote erreicht 94,5 Prozent

Im Jahr 2025 konnte Rewindo die Menge der thermischen Verwertung von PVC-Altfenstern in Müllverbrennungsanlagen gegenüber 2024 halbieren. Dies steht im Einklang mit den umweltpolitischen Zielen der Bundesregierung, die sich in den Vorgaben des Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetzes und der Gewerbeabfallverordnung widerspiegeln. Die Recyclingquote für erfassbare und verfügbare Altfenster stieg im selben Zeitraum auf 94,5 Prozent, nach 87 Prozent im Jahr 2024. Der Ergebnisbericht für die Recyclingmengen 2025 wurde von Conversio erstellt und von ecocycle unabhängig überprüft und auditiert.

## Einsparungen bei CO2 und Energie

Der Materialkreislauf für PVC-Altfenster trägt zur Ressourcenschonung bei und reduziert den CO2-Fußabdruck sowie den Energieverbrauch. Eine Studie von myclimate für Rewindo zeigt, dass eine Tonne Rezyklat Einsparungen von zwei Tonnen CO2 und 14.600 KWh Strom ermöglicht. Auf das Jahr 2025 umgerechnet, wurden durch Rewindo und seine Partner 283.200 Tonnen CO2 und über zwei Millionen KWh elektrische Energie eingespart.

Die gewonnenen Rezyklate fanden zu 70 Prozent im Großteil bei der Produktion neuer PVC-Fensterprofile Verwendung. Weitere 20 Prozent wurden zur Herstellung von PVC-Rohren eingesetzt, und 10 Prozent entfielen auf sonstige Profilanwendungen.

## Gründe für das Wachstum und Ausblick

Michael Vetter, Geschäftsführer von Rewindo, führt die Zuwachsraten auf mehrere Faktoren zurück. Dazu gehören ein Anstieg energetischer Sanierungen und Abbruchprojekte. Wohnungsunternehmen legen demnach aufgrund des aktuellen Marktumfeldes im Neubau verstärkt den Fokus auf den Gebäudebestand. Ein weiterer entscheidender Faktor war der Ausbau des Rewindo-Netzwerkes und der Recyclingpartnerschaften entlang der Wertschöpfungskette für PVC-Fenster. Zudem wurde die Anzahl der Annahmestellen für kleinere oder Kleinstmengen von PVC-Altfenstern auf bundesweit über 100 erweitert. Dieses Bring-System ergänzte das Hol-System der Recyclingpartner und erhöhte die verfügbare Altfenstermenge.

Für die kommenden Jahre erwartet das Unternehmen ein weiteres Wachstum, jedoch voraussichtlich nicht in der Größenordnung des Jahres 2025. Vetter betont, dass der energetische Sanierungsbedarf im Gebäudebestand hoch ist und Potenzial für die Zukunft bietet. Gesetzliche Vorgaben und Klimaziele beschleunigen diese Entwicklung, wovon auch die PVC-Fensterbranche profitiert. Die Branche bietet Produkte an, die Lösungen für die Transformation des Gebäudebestandes bereitstellen.

Rewindo recorded a growth of 32.3 percent in the recycling quantities of PVC old windows and related products in 2025. The recycling rate reached 94.5 percent.

Rewindo GmbH, a window recycling service based in Bonn, reported a significant increase in recycling volumes for the year 2025. With a growth of 32.3 percent, this marks the highest growth rate since the company was founded in 2002. A total of 141,595 tons of PVC old windows and related products were recycled, up from 131,000 tons the previous year.

In the area of post-consumer products, according to Recovinyl (Database RecoTraceTM), 58,358 tons of PVC old windows, shutters and related products were recorded. This represents an increase compared to the 44,109 tons in 2024. Additionally, 83,237 tons of production and processing waste were generated. The company is contributing to the achievement of the recycling targets set by VinylPlus®, the self-commitment of the European PVC industry.

In 2025, Rewindo was able to halve the amount of thermal recovery from PVC old windows in waste incineration plants compared to 2024. This aligns with the environmental policy targets of the federal government, as reflected in the regulations of the Circular Economy Act and the Commercial Waste Ordinance. The recycling rate for collectable and available old windows increased in the same period to 94.5 percent, up from 87 percent in 2024. The result report for the recycling volumes in 2025 was created by Conversio and independently verified and audited by ecocycle.

The material cycle for PVC old windows contributes to resource conservation and reduces the carbon footprint as well as energy consumption. A study by myclimate for Rewindo shows that one ton of recyclate saves two tons of CO2 and 14,600 kWh of electricity. For the year 2025, Rewindo and its partners saved 283,200 tons of CO2 and over two million kWh of electric energy.

The obtained recyclates were used 70 percent for the production of new PVC window profiles. Another 20 percent were used for the production of PVC pipes, and 10 percent were allocated to other profile applications.

Michael Vetter, Managing Director of Rewindo, attributes the growth rates to several factors. These include an increase in energy refurbishments and demolition projects. According to him, housing companies are increasingly focusing on the existing building stock due to the current market environment in new construction. Another crucial factor was the expansion of the Rewindo network and recycling partnerships along the value chain for PVC windows. Furthermore, the number of acceptance points for smaller or smallest quantities of PVC old windows has been extended to over 100 nationwide. This system complements the pick-up system of the recycling partners and increased the available quantity of old windows.

In the coming years, the company expects further growth, although probably not to the same extent as in 2025. Vetter emphasizes that the demand for energy retrofitting in the existing building stock is high and offers potential for the future. Legal requirements and climate goals accelerate this development, which also benefits the PVC window industry. The industry offers products that provide solutions for the transformation of the existing building stock.

# Roto Patio Alversa: Mo­du­la­res Sys­tem für die Fer­ti­gung von Schie­be­ele­men­ten

09.09.2026
\| [Druckvorschau](https://www.glaswelt.de/node/264408/print "Druckvorschau")

Roto Patio Alversa bietet Fensterherstellern ein modulares Beschlagsystem für Schiebeelemente, das durch Gleichteile und schlanke Prozesse die Fertigung optimiert.

![Mit der Beschlagvariante „Roto Patio Alversa | PS“ entsteht ein wirtschaftliches Parallelschiebeelement, das mit einer Spaltlüftung ausgerüstet werden kann. Die Spaltlüftung ebenso wie die robuste Langlebigkeit und die intuitive Bedienlogik empfehlen ein Schiebeelement mit dieser Beschlagvariante für öffentliche Räume mit wechselnden Besuchern.](https://www.glaswelt.de/sites/default/files/styles/aurora_default/public/aurora/2026/09/561225.jpeg?itok=e7CFt9B0)

Roto

Mit der Beschlagvariante „Roto Patio Alversa \| PS“ entsteht ein wirtschaftliches Parallelschiebeelement, das mit einer Spaltlüftung ausgerüstet werden kann. Die Spaltlüftung ebenso wie die robuste Langlebigkeit und die intuitive Bedienlogik empfehlen ein Schiebeelement mit dieser Beschlagvariante für öffentliche Räume mit wechselnden Besuchern.

Die anhaltend steigenden Preise für Baumaterialien und Herstellungskosten im Neubau verändern die Entscheidungsgrundlagen für Planer, Investoren und Bauherren. Der Fokus liegt vermehrt auf wirtschaftlich ausgewogenen Lösungen. Für Fensterhersteller bieten flexible und montagefreundliche Beschlagsysteme entsprechende Lösungen.

Ein Beispiel hierfür ist „Roto Patio Alversa“ für Schiebeelemente, das durch viele Gleichteile die Produktion vereinfacht und sich an preissensible Kunden richtet. Roto entwickelt und produziert alle Komponenten des Beschlagsystems selbst, mit dem Ziel, Qualität und Liefertreue zu gewährleisten.

## Vorteile für die Fertigung

Heike Holfelder, Produktmanagerin Sliding der Roto Fenster- und Türtechnologie, bezeichnet „Roto Patio Alversa“ als Problemlöser für Fensterhersteller. Das System ermögliche eine Verarbeitung in schlanken Prozessen und kombiniere die Vorteile der Drehkipp-Technologie für die Dichtigkeit mit dem Komfort großer Schiebeelemente. Schiebeelemente bieten viel Tageslicht, eine raumsparende Öffnung und flexiblen Lüftungskomfort, was ihre Empfehlung in verschiedenen Preissegmenten begründet.

![Der modulare Aufbau des Beschlagsystems „Roto Patio Alversa“ entlastet Fertigung, Montage, Lagerhaltung und Logistik. Bis zu vier Varianten entstehen ohne große Umbauten und mit vielen Gleichteilen auf einer Linie. Roto

Der modulare Aufbau des Beschlagsystems „Roto Patio Alversa“ entlastet Fertigung, Montage, Lagerhaltung und Logistik. Bis zu vier Varianten entstehen ohne große Umbauten und mit vielen Gleichteilen auf einer Linie. Nur wenige Bauteile werden bei höheren Ansprüchen an Bedien- und Lüftungskomfort oder Einbruchschutz ergänzt.

## Modulares System mit vielen Gleichteilen

Der modulare Aufbau des Beschlagsystems entlastet Fertigung, Montage, Lagerhaltung und Logistik. Bis zu vier Varianten entstehen ohne größere Umbauten und mit vielen Gleichteilen auf einer Linie. Komponenten wie Laufwerke, Zentralverschluss, Gleitscheren, Schienenset und Griffhebel sind bei allen Varianten identisch. Hersteller, die bereits mit „Roto NX“ oder „Roto AL“ arbeiten, verfügen über die meisten dieser Komponenten bereits im Lager, da sie auch für die Fertigung von Drehkippelementen verwendet werden. Nur wenige Bauteile müssen für höhere Ansprüche an Bedien- und Lüftungskomfort oder Einbruchschutz ergänzt werden. Dies führt zu einer wirtschaftlich effizienten Schiebetürlösung.

## Komfortoptionen für vielfältige Anwendungen

Das „Alversa“-Beschlagssystem ist für alle Rahmenmaterialien und für Flügel bis 200 kg verfügbar. Es ermöglicht die Fertigung von Schiebeelementen mit Kipp- oder Spaltlüftung.

- **„Alversa \| KS“** ist die Einsteigervariante als Kippschiebebeschlag.

- **„Alversa \| PS Air“** bietet als Parallel-Kipp-Schiebevariante zusätzlichen Komfort durch eine integrierte Öffnungsdämpfung.

- **„Alversa \| PS Air Com“** richtet sich an den privaten Wohnbereich und bietet eine griffgesteuerte Komfortlüftung: Durch Drehen des Griffhebels wird der Flügel automatisch gekippt, ein manuelles Ziehen am Flügel ist nicht erforderlich.

Die Beschlagvariante „Alversa \| PS“ ermöglicht ein Parallelschiebeelement, das optional mit einer Spaltlüftung ausgestattet werden kann. Diese Funktion erlaubt eine dauerhafte Belüftung eines Raumes, auch wenn das Element beispielsweise im einbruchgefährdeten Erdgeschoss montiert ist, da der umlaufend abgestellte Flügel von außen verschlossen wirkt. Die Spaltlüftung, die Langlebigkeit und die intuitive Bedienung empfehlen Schiebeelemente mit „Alversa \| PS“ auch für öffentliche Räume.

![Kabelgebundene Lösungen wie das magnetische Verschluss- und Öffnungsüberwachungs-System „Roto E-Tec Control | MVS“ (im Bild) sind kompatibel mit „Alversa“-Schiebebeschlägen. Gleiches gilt für Sensoren aus dem Programm „Roto Com-Tec“, die per Funk über den Öffnungsstatus informieren. Durch das weit verbreitete EnOcean-Funkprotokoll können sie in gängige Smart-Home-Systeme integriert werden. ](https://www.glaswelt.de/sites/default/files/styles/aurora_default/public/aurora/2026/09/561228.jpeg?itok=pEFCldyk)

Roto / Tom Brunner

Kabelgebundene Lösungen wie das magnetische Verschluss- und Öffnungsüberwachungs-System „Roto E-Tec Control \| MVS“ (im Bild) sind kompatibel mit „Alversa“-Schiebebeschlägen. Gleiches gilt für Sensoren aus dem Programm „Roto Com-Tec“, die per Funk über den Öffnungsstatus informieren. Durch das weit verbreitete EnOcean-Funkprotokoll können sie in gängige Smart-Home-Systeme integriert werden.

## Einbruchschutz und Smart-Home-Integration

Jedes „Alversa“-Schiebeelement kann mit „Roto Quadro Safe“-Sicherheitskomponenten wie Sicherheitspilzzapfen, Sicherheitsschließstücken und einem abschließbaren Griff bis zur Widerstandsklasse RC 2 ausgestattet werden. Die Überwachung von Verschluss- und Öffnungszustand übernehmen Sensoren aus dem Programm „Roto Com-Tec“, die Informationen per Funk übertragen. Der Status ist jederzeit via App abrufbar. Für die Integration in kabelgebundene Überwachungssysteme kann ein „Alversa“-Element mit „Roto E-Tec \| Control“ verbunden werden. Dies ermöglicht eine flexible Anpassung des Einbruchschutzes an individuelle Sicherheitsbedürfnisse und bestehende Gebäudeinstallationen. Die Sensoren mit EnOcean-Funkprotokoll sind zudem in gängige Smart-Home-Systeme integrierbar.

## Einheitliche Griffdesigns

Die Griffe für „Alversa“-Schiebeelemente sind in drei Designs verfügbar, die den Drehkipp-Griffen von Roto entsprechen: „Roto Line“, „Roto Swing“ und ab Herbst 2026 „Roto Square“. Die Bedienung aller „Alversa“-Schiebetürvarianten erfolgt analog zu Drehkipp-Fenstern.

Roto Patio Alversa offers window manufacturers a modular fitting system for sliding elements that optimizes production through uniform parts and streamlined processes.

With the fitting variant “Roto Patio Alversa | PS”, an economical parallel sliding element is created, which can be equipped with a gap ventilation. This gap ventilation, as well as the robust durability and intuitive operation make this sliding element variant suitable for public spaces with changing visitors.

The rising prices for building materials and manufacturing costs in new construction are changing the decision-making basis for planners, investors, and builders. The focus increasingly lies on economically balanced solutions. For window manufacturers, flexible and assembly-friendly fitting systems provide corresponding solutions.

One example is “Roto Patio Alversa” for sliding elements, which simplifies production through many uniform parts and is aimed at price-sensitive customers. Roto develops and produces all components of the fitting system itself, with the goal of ensuring quality and delivery reliability.

Heike Holfelder, Product Manager for Sliding at Roto Window and Door Technology, describes “Roto Patio Alversa” as a problem solver for window manufacturers. The system enables processing in streamlined processes and combines the advantages of tilt-and-turn technology for tightness with the comfort of large sliding elements. Sliding elements provide plenty of daylight, a space-saving opening, and flexible ventilation comfort, which justifies their recommendation in various price segments.

The modular design of the fitting system “Roto Patio Alversa” relieves production, assembly, storage, and logistics. Up to four variants can be produced without extensive modifications and with many uniform parts on one line. Only a few components will be added for higher demands on operation and ventilation comfort or burglary protection.

The modular structure of the fitting system relieves production, assembly, storage, and logistics. Up to four variants can be produced without major alterations and with many uniform parts on one line. Components such as drives, central locks, sliding scissors, rail sets, and handle levers are identical across all variants. Manufacturers already working with “Roto NX” or “Roto AL” already have most of these components in stock, as they are also used for the production of tilt-and-turn elements. Only a few components need to be added for higher demands on operation and ventilation comfort or burglary protection. This leads to an economically efficient sliding door solution.

The “Alversa” fitting system is available for all frame materials and for sashes weighing up to 200 kg. It allows the production of sliding elements with tilt or gap ventilation.

“Alversa | KS” is the entry-level variant as a tilt-slide fitting.

“Alversa | PS Air” offers additional comfort as a parallel-tilt-slide option through integrated opening damping.

“Alversa | PS Air Com” is aimed at the private residential sector and offers handle-controlled ventilation comfort: rotating the handle lever automatically tilts the sash, manual pulling on the sash is not required.

The fitting variant “Alversa | PS” enables a parallel sliding element that can optionally be equipped with a gap ventilation. This function allows for continuous ventilation of a room, even if the element is, for example, mounted on the ground floor, which is at risk of burglary, as the sashes securely appear locked from the outside. The gap ventilation, long-lasting durability, and intuitive operation also recommend sliding elements with “Alversa | PS” for public places.

Wired solutions such as the magnetic closing and opening monitoring system “Roto E-Tec Control | MVS” (in the picture) are compatible with “Alversa” sliding fittings. The same applies to sensors from the “Roto Com-Tec” program, which inform about the opening status via radio. Through the widely used EnOcean radio protocol, they can be integrated into common smart home systems.

Every “Alversa” sliding element can be equipped with “Roto Quadro Safe” security components, such as security mushroom pins, security locking pieces, and a lockable handle up to resistance class RC 2. Monitoring of the locking and opening status is managed by sensors from the “Roto Com-Tec” program, which transmit information wirelessly. The status can be accessed via app at any time. For integration into wired monitoring systems, an “Alversa” element can be connected with “Roto E-Tec | Control”. This allows for flexible adaptation of burglary protection to individual security needs and existing building installations. The sensors with EnOcean radio protocol can also be integrated into common smart home systems.

The handles for “Alversa” sliding elements are available in three designs, corresponding to the tilt-and-turn handles from Roto: “Roto Line”, “Roto Swing”, and from fall 2026 “Roto Square”. The operation of all “Alversa” sliding door variants is analogous to tilt-and-turn windows.

# Kömmerling erweitert Zubehör-Portfolio um Dr. Hahn Türbeschläge

08.09.2026
\| [Druckvorschau](https://www.glaswelt.de/node/264575/print "Druckvorschau")

![Dr. Peter Mrosik, Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter der profine Group, und Walter Back, Gesamtvertriebsleiter und Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung der Dr. Hahn GmbH & Co. KG, haben eine Kooperation bei der Unternehmen vereinbart](https://www.glaswelt.de/sites/default/files/styles/teaser_image_full__s/public/aurora/2026/09/561803.jpeg?itok=v9ky6bLB)

Kömmerling

Dr. Peter Mrosik, Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter der profine Group, und Walter Back, Gesamtvertriebsleiter und Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung der Dr. Hahn GmbH & Co. KG, haben eine Kooperation bei der Unternehmen vereinbart


Die profine Group mit ihrer Marke Kömmerling und der Türbandhersteller Dr. Hahn gehen eine strategische Vertriebskooperation ein. Seit September 2026 können Kunden Dr. Hahn Aufschraub- und Rollenbänder direkt bei Kömmerling erwerben.

(Externer Link) [GW bei Google bevorzugen](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=glaswelt.de)

"Mit Dr. Hahn haben wir einen zuverlässigen Partner gefunden. Die aktuelle Vertriebskooperation ist ein erster Schritt, um die Möglichkeit zu haben, unsere Zusammenarbeit zu vertiefen und Systemlösungen zu entwickeln, die technisch und funktional deutlich über klassische Einzelkomponenten hinausgehen", erklärt Dr. Peter Mrosik, Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter der profine Group.

Das Profilsystemhaus verfolgt mit der Partnerschaft seine Strategie, Kunden mit hochwertigem Zubehör aus einer Hand zu beliefern. Durch die Kooperation sollen normgerechte, hocheffiziente und langfristig zukunftssichere Produktlösungen im Bereich moderner Türsysteme entstehen.

Walter Back, Gesamtvertriebsleiter und Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung der Dr. Hahn GmbH & Co. KG, sieht in der Zusammenarbeit einen wichtigen Meilenstein: "Diese Kooperation bedeutet für uns einen wichtigen Meilenstein. Durch die Zusammenarbeit mit einem führenden Profilhersteller können wir unseren Kunden leistungsstarke und normgerechte Produktlösungen als durchdachte Systemlösungen anbieten." Er ergänzt: "Gemeinsam können wir Systemlösungen schaffen, die konventionelle Einzelkomponenten klar übertreffen."

## Optimale Abstimmung bereits in der Entwicklung

Die enge Verzahnung von Türband- und Profil-Technologie ermöglicht bereits in der Entwicklungsphase eine optimale Abstimmung der Produkte. Dies schaffe Raum für neue Entwicklungen und biete auch im Hinblick auf zukünftige europäische Vorgaben einen klaren Mehrwert, der nur durch gemeinsames Entwickeln erreicht werden könne, sind beide Unternehmen überzeugt.

Kömmerling expands its accessory portfolio with Dr. Hahn door fittings.

Dr. Peter Mrosik, Managing Partner of the profine Group, and Walter Back, Head of Sales and Member of the Executive Board of Dr. Hahn GmbH & Co. KG, have agreed on a cooperation between their companies.

The profine Group, with its Kömmerling brand, and the door hinge manufacturer Dr. Hahn are entering into a strategic sales cooperation. Since September 2026, customers can purchase Dr. Hahn surface-mounted and roller hinges directly from Kömmerling.

“With Dr. Hahn, we have found a reliable partner. This current sales cooperation is a first step to deepen our collaboration and develop system solutions that are technically and functionally significantly beyond classic individual components,” explains Dr. Peter Mrosik.

The profile system house is pursuing a strategy with this partnership to supply customers with high-quality accessories from a single source. The cooperation is expected to generate regulatory-compliant, highly efficient, and long-term future-proof product solutions in the field of modern door systems.

Walter Back sees this collaboration as an important milestone: “This cooperation means an important milestone for us. By working with a leading profile manufacturer, we can offer our customers powerful and regulatory-compliant product solutions as well-thought-out system solutions. Together, we can create system solutions that clearly exceed conventional individual components.”

Optimal coordination already in development

The close interplay between door hinge and profile technology allows for optimal product alignment already in the development phase. This creates room for new developments and provides a clear added value, especially concerning future European requirements, which can only be achieved through joint development.

title: Company insolvencies remain high.
summary: In Germany, the number of large bankruptcies remains high, with 209 companies filing for insolvency in the first half of 2026. This figure, while slightly lower than the previous year, exceeds the five-year average of 142 cases. Notably, the automotive suppliers led this year’s insolvency requests.

KunststoffWeb: Fachinformationen für die Kunststoffindustrie

![Leere Taschen: Die Zahl der Großinsolvenzen verharrt auf hohem Niveau (Foto: Smarterpix/nito103)](https://www.kunststoffweb.de/_assets/images/nachrichten/ki/w261022A.jpg)Leere Taschen: Die Zahl der Großinsolvenzen verharrt auf hohem Niveau (Foto: Smarterpix/nito103)

Die Zahl der Großinsolvenzen verharrt in Deutschland auf hohem Niveau. Wie die Restrukturierungsberater von Falkensteg (Düsseldorf) in ihrem aktuellen Insolvenzreport „5-nach-12“ berichten, haben insgesamt 209 Unternehmen mit einem Umsatz von mehr als 10 Mio EUR im ersten Halbjahr 2026 einen Insolvenzantrag gestellt. Das waren zwar acht Verfahren weniger als in den ersten sechs Monaten des Vorjahres, aber die Zahl lag damit weiterhin deutlich über dem Fünfjahres-Durchschnitt von 142 Fällen.

An kunststoffrelevanten Großunternehmen erfassten die Falkensteg-Experten insgesamt zwölf Insolvenzanträge und damit einen mehr als im Jahr zuvor. Bei den diesjährigen Fällen rangierten die Automobilzulieferer ganz vorne.

The number of major insolvencies in Germany remains at a high level. According to the restructuring consultants from Falkensteg (Düsseldorf) in their current insolvency report “5-nach-12”, a total of 209 companies with sales of more than 10 million EUR filed for insolvency in the first half of 2026. Among major companies relevant to plastics, Falkensteg’s experts recorded a total of twelve insolvency filings, one more than the previous year. In this year’s cases, the automotive suppliers ranked first.

title: Aramco considers Arlanxeo sale.
summary: Saudi Aramco is considering selling stakes worth approximately $35 billion, including the elastomer producer Arlanxeo. The state-owned oil company has reportedly engaged J.P. Morgan for the sale, aiming for revenue estimates of €2.9 billion for Arlanxeo in 2026. Initial inquiries to both companies for confirmation received no responses.
content:
KunststoffWeb: Fachinformationen für die Kunststoffindustrie

![Vor Eignerwechsel? Elastomer-Erzeugung in Dormagen (Foto: Arlanxeo)](https://www.kunststoffweb.de/_assets/images/nachrichten/ki/w261033A.jpg)Vor Eignerwechsel? Elastomer-Erzeugung in Dormagen (Foto: Arlanxeo)

Offensichtlich tritt Saudi Aramco (Dhahran / Saudi-Arabien) finanziell auf die Bremse: Nach Angaben der Nachrichtenagentur „Bloomberg“ prüft der staatliche saudische Ölkonzern Verkäufe von Beteiligungen im Wert von insgesamt rund 35 Mrd USD (30 Mrd EUR). Angedacht sei auch eine Abgabe des Elastomerherstellers Arlanxeo (Maastricht / Niederlande), schreibt Bloomberg und beruft sich auf mit dem Vorgang vertraute Quellen. Weder Arlanxeo noch Saudi Aramco antworteten zunächst auf entsprechende KI-Nachfragen.

Dem Vernehmen nach hat Aramco bereits im Juli 2026 die US-Investmentbank J.P. Morgan unter dem Decknamen „Projekt Atlas“ mit dem Verkauf beauftragt. Dabei werden für Arlanxeo ein Umsatz von 2,9 Mrd EUR sowie ein geschätztes Ebitda von 140 Mio EUR für das Jahr 2026 angegeben. Saudi Aramco selbst nennt keine Zahlen zu einzelnen Beteiligungen.

KunststoffWeb: Industry Insights for the Plastics Industry

Facing a change of ownership? Elastomer Production in Dormagen.

Saudi Aramco is clearly hitting the brakes financially: According to Bloomberg news agency, the state-owned Saudi oil giant is reviewing the sale of stakes totaling approximately $35 billion USD. The sale of the elastomer manufacturer Arlanxeo is also planned, Bloomberg reports, citing sources familiar with the matter. Neither Arlanxeo nor Saudi Aramco initially responded to corresponding AI inquiries.

It is said that Aramco commissioned J.P. Morgan under the codename Project Atlas as early as July 2026 to handle the sale of Arlanxeo. The figures cited include a turnover of EUR 2.9 billion and an estimated EBITDA of EUR 140 million for 2026 for Arlanxeo. Saudi Aramco does not provide figures for individual stakes.

title: BASF starts new plant
summary: Schütz is investing over €40 million in a new production and logistics center for Intermediate Bulk Containers in Ludwigshafen, with construction starting on September 14, 2026. The facility will create approximately 60 jobs initially, expanding to 100 in later stages. The center aims to serve BASF and other industrial customers in the Rhine-Neckar region.
content:
KunststoffWeb: Fachinformationen für die Kunststoffindustrie

![Offizieller Spatenstich: Veit Enders (Vorstandsmitglied Schütz), Prof. Dr. Klaus Blettner (Oberbürgermeister der Stadt Ludwigshafen), Helmut Winterling (Leiter der europäischen Verbundstandorte bei BASF), Udo Schütz (Gründer der Schütz-Gruppe), Uwe Lohr (Leiter des weltweiten Einkaufs von Dienstleistungen und nicht produktionsbezogenen Gütern bei BASF), Roland Straßburger (Vorstandsvorsitzender Schütz) und Matthias Dohrn (Leiter des weltweiten Einkaufs bei BASF; v.li; Foto: Schütz)](https://www.kunststoffweb.de/_assets/images/nachrichten/ki/w261018A.jpg)Offizieller Spatenstich: Veit Enders (Vorstandsmitglied Schütz), Prof. Dr. Klaus Blettner (Oberbürgermeister der Stadt Ludwigshafen), Helmut Winterling (Leiter der europäischen Verbundstandorte bei BASF), Udo Schütz (Gründer der Schütz-Gruppe), Uwe Lohr (Leiter des weltweiten Einkaufs von Dienstleistungen und nicht produktionsbezogenen Gütern bei BASF), Roland Straßburger (Vorstandsvorsitzender Schütz) und Matthias Dohrn (Leiter des weltweiten Einkaufs bei BASF; v.li; Foto: Schütz)

Der Hersteller von Industriepackmitteln Schütz (Selters) investiert mehr als 40 Mio EUR in ein Produktions- und Logistikzentrum für Intermediate Bulk Container (IBC) in Ludwigshafen. Mit dem Spatenstich am 14. September 2026 haben die Bauarbeiten offiziell begonnen; die Inbetriebnahme ist für Sommer 2027 geplant.

Auf einer Fläche von rund 20.000 m² unmittelbar neben dem BASF-Stammwerk sollen künftig IBC produziert und gelagert werden. Schütz will zunächst rund 60 neue Arbeitsplätze schaffen, in späteren Ausbaustufen sollen es bis zu 100 sein. Neben BASF sollen von Ludwigshafen aus auch weitere Industriekunden in der Rhein-Neckar-Region beliefert werden.

Industrial Packaging Manufacturer Schütz is investing more than 40 million EUR in a production and logistics center for Intermediate Bulk Containers in Ludwigshafen. Construction began officially with the groundbreaking on September 14, 2026; commissioning is planned for summer 2027.

On an area of approximately 20,000 m² directly adjacent to the BASF headquarters, IBCs will be produced and stored in the future. title: Trinseo raises PMMA prices.
summary: Trinseo is announcing a price increase for PMMA under the 'Altuglas' brand, raising prices by €250 per ton starting October 1, 2026. This increase will affect the European, Middle Eastern, and African markets. The change reflects ongoing market dynamics and cost pressures in the plastics industry.

title: Alpla expands Turkish operations.
summary: Alpla, an Austrian packaging manufacturer, is expanding its production facilities in Turkey with a €30 million investment in new locations in Izmir and Adana. The Izmir plant will produce PET preforms and bottles, while the Adana facility focuses on PET and HDPE packaging. Both sites aim to serve clients in the beverage, food, dairy, and personal care industries.
content:
KunststoffWeb: Fachinformationen für die Kunststoffindustrie

![Zur Eröffnung des neuen Werks im türkischen Adana am 14. September kamen Emre Canoglu (Geschäftsführer Alpla Türkei), Javier Delgado (Regionalgeschäftsführer für Afrika, Nahost und die Türkei), Philipp Lehner (CEO) und Walter Ritzer (COO) zusammen (v.li., Foto: Alpla)](https://www.kunststoffweb.de/_assets/images/nachrichten/ki/w261026A.jpg)Zur Eröffnung des neuen Werks im türkischen Adana am 14. September kamen Emre Canoglu (Geschäftsführer Alpla Türkei), Javier Delgado (Regionalgeschäftsführer für Afrika, Nahost und die Türkei), Philipp Lehner (CEO) und Walter Ritzer (COO) zusammen (v.li., Foto: Alpla)

Der österreichische Verpackungshersteller Alpla (Hard / Österreich) baut die Produktionskapazitäten in der Türkei aus. Rund 30 Mio EUR hat das Unternehmen in zwei neue Standorte in Izmir an der türkischen Ägäisküste sowie in Adana im Süden des Landes investiert.

Das Werk in Izmir verfügt über eine Produktionsfläche von rund 50.000 m² und fertigt PET-Preforms, Verschlüsse sowie fertige Flaschen aus Polyethylen-HD und PET. Der mit 20.000 m² kleinere Standort in Adana konzentriert sich auf PET-Preforms sowie Verpackungen aus PE-HD und Polypropylen. Beide Werke beliefern Kunden aus der Getränke-, Lebensmittel- und Molkereiindustrie sowie Hersteller von Haushalts- und Körperpflegeprodukten.

At the opening of the new plant in Adana, Turkey, on September 14, Emre Canoglu (Managing Director of Alpla Turkey), Javier Delgado (Regional Manager for Africa, Middle East, and Turkey), Philipp Lehner (CEO), and Walter Ritzer (COO) gathered together.

The Austrian packaging manufacturer Alpla is expanding its production capacities in Turkey. The company has invested around 30 million EUR in two new locations in Izmir on the Turkish Aegean coast and in Adana in the south of the country.

The plant in Izmir has a production area of approximately 50,000 square meters and manufactures PET preforms, closures, and finished bottles made of polyethylene HD and PET. The smaller site in Adana, which is 20,000 square meters, focuses on PET preforms and packaging made of PE HD and polypropylene. Both plants serve customers in the beverage, food, and dairy industries as well as manufacturers of household and personal care products.

title: UBA pays out funds.
summary: The German Federal Environment Agency (UBA) has established a point value for the initial payout from the single-use plastics fund, amounting to €0.274 per point for 2024. This fund will distribute approximately €205 million to municipalities for waste collection and management. Since January 2024, manufacturers of specific single-use plastic products have been required to contribute to the cost of waste disposal in public spaces.

Grundlage ist das Einwegkunststofffondsgesetz (EWKFondsG), mit dem die erweiterte Herstellerverantwortung umgesetzt wird.

Cost factor public space: Municipalities receive money from the single-use plastic fund for the collection and disposal of certain waste.

The Federal Environment Agency (UBA, Dessau) has set the point value for the first payout from the single-use plastic fund. For the reporting year 2024, it amounts to 0.274 EUR per point. This will transfer around 205 million EUR to municipalities and public disposal authorities that have provided services for cleaning the public space as well as for the collection and disposal of waste. 

Since January 2024, manufacturers and sellers of certain single-use plastic products in Germany must bear part of the costs for their disposal in public spaces. This is based on the Single-Use Plastic Fund Act (EWKFondsG), which implements extended producer responsibility.

# The Unresolved Trade: Why Getting Technology Onto the Plans is Not Enough

How integrators can move upstream in construction by focusing on human experience, design intent and coordinated technology that supports life inside the space.

Published: September 21, 2026Jimmy Powers

![Featured Image](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/21B5792F-1BEE-4BDD-AD5F-CD669EBB4A35-e1790019191828.jpeg)

Photos courtesy of Blend Technology

Our industry has spent years talking about getting involved earlier in construction.

The concern is valid. By the time many integrators arrive, walls are framed, mechanical systems are laid out, lighting decisions are made, and the interior designer is finalizing finishes. Decisions that directly affect our work have already been locked in.

Technology should be formally included alongside mechanical, electrical, and plumbing. MEP should be MEPT. In many parts of the industry, it already is.

But adding the T is not enough.

If technology means only pathways, wiring, racks, speakers, screens, and equipment locations, we may arrive earlier without becoming more valuable. The greater opportunity is not simply getting technology onto the plans. It is defining what technology should do for the people inside the building.

## **The Habit That Limits Us**

![](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/D78AD8D6-CF6A-4AD8-B12A-4CA1FEB90766-e1790019775824.jpeg)

Consider a typical job walk.

The MEP work is underway. The framer is active. The interior designer is working through finishes. The general contractor brought us in because the client requested us, or because the GC trusts us. We enter what will become the primary bedroom and ask a familiar question:

“Do you want speakers in this room?”

The client says, “We barely listen to music.”

The bedroom comes off the distributed audio plan, and everyone moves on.

The decision feels reasonable. But we did not simply remove a pair of speakers. We removed every experience the client might have valued individually.

Would sound masking help protect sleep from doors closing down the hall? Should the doorbell be audible upstairs without becoming disruptive? Could the room support meditation, reading, or a nighttime wind-down? Would a controlled soundscape help someone rest while the rest of the house remains active? None of those are music questions. All of them are audio decisions. Different question, different answer, same room.

## **One Good Question Changes the Project**

An experiential question rarely stays inside one system. Suppose the client tells us that protecting sleep is important in the primary bedroom.

The speakers may now require isolated back boxes rather than open joist cavities that transmit sound through the structure. That decision affects framing, pathways, and mechanical coordination before the ceiling is closed.

If the doorbell needs to be heard in the bedroom at a controlled level and only at appropriate times, the entry system must communicate with the audio system. Security and audio can no longer be treated as unrelated packages.

Sleep also does not begin at the pillow. Evening lighting may need to become warmer and lower as the day ends. Shades may need to respond to dusk and morning light. That becomes a lighting, electrical, shading, and programming conversation before rough-in is complete.

Mechanical systems matter as well. Low-velocity air, quieter equipment, nighttime temperature targets, and schedules that begin before bedtime all influence whether the room actually supports rest. Those requirements must be coordinated before the duct layout is fixed.

One meaningful question in one bedroom can place the integrator in conversation with the framer, electrician, HVAC contractor, interior designer, and other trades. Not because we are trying to control their work, but because the outcome the client cares about crosses all of it.

## **What Upstream Actually Means**

![](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Sweet-e1790019693148.jpg)

Being upstream does not simply mean arriving earlier on the calendar. It means bringing questions that ripple across the building, understanding where those ripples land, and documenting them before they become field conflicts.

Integrators touch more systems in a modern building than nearly any other subtrade. We coordinate audio, video, networks, lighting control, shading, climate, access, alarm, surveillance, leak detection, energy monitoring, sensing, and automation.

Our work also intersects directly with framing, millwork, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, interior finishes, acoustical isolation, and architectural details. That reach should give our trade an important position. But reach alone does not earn it.

## **We Have to Think and Document Like Designers**

Designers do not begin with products. They begin with intent.

An architect does not ask whether the client wants walls. The architect asks how the client wants to live, then designs walls, circulation, light, scale, and proportion around that life. Our trade needs to move the same way.

The vocabulary must shift from what should be installed to what the space should do.

Then intent must be translated into measurable performance and coordinated documentation: system behaviors, sensor strategies, acoustic requirements, infrastructure drawings, trade dependencies, control logic, commissioning criteria, and the construction phase in which each decision must be made.

A rack elevation is useful. A wire schedule is necessary. Neither, by itself, is a design methodology. A product list earns a vendor’s seat. A design earns a designer’s seat.

## **Our Best Attempt at the Work**

![](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/B71E88E0-3308-455B-9B16-39F01489A00D-e1790019820164.jpeg)

At Blend, we call our process [UX for Spaces™.](https://ux-for-spaces.blend.technology/ux-for-spaces)

It begins by defining how a building should perceive, anticipate, respond, offer control, and adapt to the people inside it. Those principles move the work beyond automation and toward a clear behavioral standard for the built environment.

The Calm Tech Institute helped us understand how broad this work can become. Technology affects attention, mood, sleep, cognition, and biological rhythms. The institute’s principles ask technology to respect attention, operate in the periphery, transition calmly, and continue serving people when something fails.

We are working with the Calm Tech Institute to turn those ideas into a design discipline that can be documented, coordinated, commissioned, and verified.

This is the structure we believe can move the work forward and help the trade earn a more meaningful role in the built environment.

## **The Conversation We Want to Join**

We want to be part of the conversation about the future of this trade, and that conversation has to begin with the value we are actually delivering.

No single company will define that future. It will take integrators, architects, builders, engineers, designers, manufacturers, and other professionals willing to reconsider the role technology plays in the built environment.

The question is not simply how we get invited earlier. It is what we are prepared to contribute when we arrive.

In the end, the rack disappears. The interface disappears. The product line disappears. What remains is the bedroom where someone finally sleeps through the night. The dining room that holds birthdays, holidays, difficult conversations, and the ordinary family dinners people will one day miss. The workplace where someone can think clearly enough to do the work that matters. The wellness space where a body carrying too much stress can finally let go. The restaurant table where people fall in love, raise a glass, repair what was broken, or find the courage to say the words that change everything after them.

Technology is not the meaning of those moments. It is the quiet infrastructure that supports and protects them. Systems are how we make those moments possible. Life inside the room is what we are actually delivering.

* * *

_Jimmy Powers is founder and principal of [Blend Technology.](https://www.blend.technology/about-blend-technology)_

The Unresolved Trade: Why Getting Technology Onto the Plans is Not Enough

How integrators can move upstream in construction by focusing on human experience, design intent, and coordinated technology that supports life inside the space.

Published: September 21, 2026

Our industry has spent years talking about getting involved earlier in construction.

The concern is valid. By the time many integrators arrive, walls are framed, mechanical systems are laid out, lighting decisions are made, and the interior designer is finalizing finishes. Decisions that directly affect our work have already been locked in.

Technology should be formally included alongside mechanical, electrical, and plumbing. MEP should be MEPT. In many parts of the industry, it already is.

But adding the T is not enough.

If technology means only pathways, wiring, racks, speakers, screens, and equipment locations, we may arrive earlier without becoming more valuable. The greater opportunity is not simply getting technology onto the plans. It is defining what technology should do for the people inside the building.

The Habit That Limits Us

Consider a typical job walk.

The MEP work is underway. The framer is active. The interior designer is working through finishes. The general contractor brought us in because the client requested us, or because the GC trusts us. We enter what will become the primary bedroom and ask a familiar question:

“Do you want speakers in this room?”

The client says, “We barely listen to music.”

The bedroom comes off the distributed audio plan, and everyone moves on.

The decision feels reasonable. But we did not simply remove a pair of speakers. We removed every experience the client might have valued individually.

Would sound masking help protect sleep from doors closing down the hall? Should the doorbell be audible upstairs without becoming disruptive? Could the room support meditation, reading, or a nighttime wind-down? Would a controlled soundscape help someone rest while the rest of the house remains active? None of those are music questions. All of them are audio decisions. Different question, different answer, same room.

One Good Question Changes the Project

An experiential question rarely stays inside one system. Suppose the client tells us that protecting sleep is important in the primary bedroom.

The speakers may now require isolated back boxes rather than open joist cavities that transmit sound through the structure. That decision affects framing, pathways, and mechanical coordination before the ceiling is closed.

If the doorbell needs to be heard in the bedroom at a controlled level and only at appropriate times, the entry system must communicate with the audio system. Security and audio can no longer be treated as unrelated packages.

Sleep also does not begin at the pillow. Evening lighting may need to become warmer and lower as the day ends. Shades may need to respond to dusk and morning light. That becomes a lighting, electrical, shading, and programming conversation before rough-in is complete.

Mechanical systems matter as well. Low-velocity air, quieter equipment, nighttime temperature targets, and schedules that begin before bedtime all influence whether the room actually supports rest. Those requirements must be coordinated before the duct layout is fixed.

One meaningful question in one bedroom can place the integrator in conversation with the framer, electrician, HVAC contractor, interior designer, and other trades. Not because we are trying to control their work, but because the outcome the client cares about crosses all of it.

What Upstream Actually Means

Being upstream does not simply mean arriving earlier on the calendar. It means bringing questions that ripple across the building, understanding where those ripples land, and documenting them before they become field conflicts.

Integrators touch more systems in a modern building than nearly any other subtrade. We coordinate audio, video, networks, lighting control, shading, climate, access, alarm, surveillance, leak detection, energy monitoring, sensing, and automation.

Our work also intersects directly with framing, millwork, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, interior finishes, acoustical isolation, and architectural details. That reach should give our trade an important position. But reach alone does not earn it.

We Have to Think and Document Like Designers

Designers do not begin with products. They begin with intent.

An architect does not ask whether the client wants walls. The architect asks how the client wants to live, then designs walls, circulation, light, scale, and proportion around that life. Our trade needs to move the same way.

The vocabulary must shift from what should be installed to what the space should do.

Then intent must be translated into measurable performance and coordinated documentation: system behaviors, sensor strategies, acoustic requirements, infrastructure drawings, trade dependencies, control logic, commissioning criteria, and the construction phase in which each decision must be made.

# Integration Controls Unveils New Buying Tool for Clients Addressing Industry Pain Points

Shop the Look aims to make the buying process more approachable for prospective integration clients by providing a ‘common vocabulary’ for project scope and pricing.

Published: September 21, 2026Nick Boever

![Photo of environment in Shop the Look](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/ShoptheLook.jpg)

Photo courtesy of Integration Controls

Integration Controls is launching a new tool for its customers aimed at making the buying process for home technology upgrades much simpler. Calling it “Shop the Look,” Integration Controls says it’s a first-of-its-kind digital planning experience to help its clients understand what’s possible (and what it costs) before the design process begins.

“Consumers today expect to research major purchases before they ever schedule a consultation,” said Jamie Briesemeister, co-founder and CEO of Integration Controls. “At the same time, it’s often a challenge for those unfamiliar with technology to visualize how it will look and function in their home, with their aesthetic and lifestyle in mind.

“We asked luxury designers and builders in the St. Louis area which interior styles were most common, and we designed a resource that matches different styles, whether it’s Mid-century or French modern.  Shop the Look provides a consistent way to visualize personalized home technology solutions, bringing our clients’ concepts to life.”

## What Shop the Look Aims to Provide for Custom Integration

According to Integration Controls, Shop the Look allows homeowners to explore curated levels of home technology from the comfort of their home, office or while meeting with design/build professionals for a project.

The platform organizes home technology into categories and tiers that are more intuitive to the average buyer, from foundational one-room technologies to fully bespoke, whole-home systems. This further allows users to compare different levels of performance across different price points while also exploring how different systems will appear in a variety of home styles.

#### Why Integrators Should Take Note

While developed to improve Integration Controls’ own client experience, Shop the Look addresses a challenge familiar to integrators across the industry: translating complex technology systems into an experience clients can easily understand.

In a way, the tool works to establish a common vocabulary, sometimes even before the first consultation, by giving everyone a clearer understanding of available solutions, investment options and lifestyle outcomes, reducing uncertainty and establishing more realistic expectations in the process.

“We built Shop the Look to solve a challenge within our own business,” Briesemeister added. “The preliminary response we’ve received from our manufacturer partners and other integrators suggests this isn’t just our challenge—it’s an industry challenge. For over 20 years, we have led with ‘experience-first’ and now, we have the ability to help our clients visualize what that means earlier in the process.  It’s an opportunity to rethink how clients are introduced to technology, ultimately making the buying experience better for everyone.”

### Where to See Shop the Look

For anyone looking to explore the tool themselves, Shop the Look is available now at integrationcontrols.com.

However, the launch also coincides with the Grand Opening of Integration Controls’ new Technology Design Center, located at 10164 Watson Rd in Sunset Hills, Missouri. There attendees will get in-person access to Shop the Look.

On Friday, October 2, 2026, from 4 to 7 pm, a private VIP preview will host design/build partners, realtors, and other business connections to explore the design center and ‘Shop the Look’ in person.

This will be followed by a community-wide Open House on Saturday, October 3, 2026, for the Sunset Hills and surrounding communities to visit.

To RSVP or learn more about the event, readers are instructed to either [click here](https://integrationcontrols.zohobackstage.com/DesignCenterPublicGrandOpening#/) or reach out to Vickie Hayden at vhayden@integrationcontrols.com.

# Audio Advice to Grow Sales Team in Response to Further National Expansion

Following a period of significant company growth, Audio Advice will be adding and relocating several personnel to keep pace with service and expertise.

Published: September 21, 2026Nick Boever

![Sony RGB](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Sony-wallAudioAdviceShowroom-1.jpg)

Interior, Audio Advice Showroom. Photo courtesy of Audio Advice

Following a period of [significant company growth and market expansion](https://www.cepro.com/news/audio-advice-expands-national-footprint-with-acquisition-of-the-sound-room/621168/), Audio Advice has announced it will be “beefing up” its sales force to continue to provide the level of customer service and product expertise that has earned the firm its national reputation in both custom integration (CI) and consumer electronics.

As part of this growth, Audio Advice is adding two key salespeople to its [Miami location](https://www.cepro.com/news/audio-advice-adds-sound-components-to-growing-family-of-national-locations/627354/): Sebastian Simon and Aleksei Panov.

Simon is a Miami local with deep ties to the community, while Panov has served Audio Advice’s Charlotte location for many years. As part of this new position, Panov will relocate to support the growing Miami team under Simon. Audio Advice says his extensive background in premium A/V solutions will be an immediate asset to the rapidly expanding Miami customer base.

Concurrent with strengthening the Miami team, Audio Advice is also welcoming industry veteran Chad Fagin to its Charlotte location. Fagin brings several decades of specialized experience in both high-performance audio and advanced home automation. Audio Advice says his vast knowledge will further elevate the premium, custom-tailored experiences that Charlotte-area clients have come to expect.

#### Why Integrators Should Take Note

These strategic personnel moves represent Audio Advice’s ongoing approach to growth across North America, ensuring that, as the company expands, its customer service retains the same level of quality and care that a more local business would have.

“As home technology becomes increasingly sophisticated, Audio Advice recognizes that the foundation of an exceptional customer experience lies in the expertise of its staff,” says the company in a press release.

Audio Advice to Grow Sales Team in Response to Further National Expansion

Following a period of significant company growth, Audio Advice will be adding and relocating several personnel to keep pace with service and expertise.

Published: September 21, 2026 Nick Boever

Following a period of significant company growth and market expansion, Audio Advice has announced it will be beefing up its sales force to continue to provide the level of customer service and product expertise that has earned the firm its national reputation in both custom integration and consumer electronics.

As part of this growth, Audio Advice is adding two key salespeople to its Miami location: Sebastian Simon and Aleksei Panov.

Simon is a Miami local with deep ties to the community, while Panov has served Audio Advice’s Charlotte location for many years. As part of this new position, Panov will relocate to support the growing Miami team under Simon. Audio Advice says his extensive background in premium A/V solutions will be an immediate asset to the rapidly expanding Miami customer base.

Concurrent with strengthening the Miami team, Audio Advice is also welcoming industry veteran Chad Fagin to its Charlotte location. Fagin brings several decades of specialized experience in both high-performance audio and advanced home automation. Audio Advice says his vast knowledge will further elevate the premium, custom-tailored experiences that Charlotte-area clients have come to expect.

These strategic personnel moves represent Audio Advice’s ongoing approach to growth across North America, ensuring that, as the company expands, its customer service retains the same level of quality and care that a more local business would have.

As home technology becomes increasingly sophisticated, Audio Advice recognizes that the foundation of an exceptional customer experience lies in the expertise of its staff.

By continually recruiting, relocating, and investing in top-tier talent like Simon, Panov, and Fagin, the company ensures that every customer—whether they are building a dedicated home theater, upgrading their two-channel audio system, or integrating full-scale home automation—receives unparalleled guidance and support.

# Z-Wave Fall Summit Unveils Programming for 2026 Outing

The event will begin with the members-only Unplug Fest before opening to the public with a Z-Wave Demo and tour of ADT’s open standard concept house.

Published: September 21, 2026Nick Boever

![Shelly Wave Z-Wave Long Range](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/zwave_transparent-1000x550-1.png)

The Z-Wave Fall Summit is coming up for 2026, and ahead of the event, the Z-Wave Alliance (referred to as the Alliance) has released greater details on the programming for attendees, both confirmed and prospective. The event kicks off September 29 with the member-only Unplug Fest, where Z-Wave Alliance members can conduct informal device-to-device interoperability testing for Z-Wave and Z-Wave Long Range (ZWLR) products, collaborate with other developers and manufacturers, and exchange knowledge across the ecosystem.

Following Unplug Fest, programming opens to integrators, installers, developers and other industry professionals. The Fall Summit will run from September 29–October 1 in Boca Raton, Florida.

#### Why Integrators Should Take Note

The Z-Wave Fall Summit is a three-day conference that brings together commercial and consumer IoT industry experts, manufacturers and practitioners for sessions spanning industry trends, market opportunities and Z-Wave technical development.

## Information and Programming for Z-Wave Fall Summit 2026

### September 29

Upon opening to the public, programming for the 2026 Z-Wave Fall Summit opens with a Z-Wave Feature Demo led by Z-Wave expert Eric Ryherd (Dr. Z-Wave). The Alliance explains that the demo will cover several Z-Wave features in action, including SmartStart commissioning, ZWLR, simultaneous Z-Wave Mesh and Z-Wave Long Range operation on the same controller, and sub-Gigahertz operation.

The day will conclude with a welcome reception—presented by Fall Summit diamond sponsor ADT—and will include a panel session discussing how open standards are shaping the future of the connected home as well as an opportunity to tour ADT’s Callahan Family Home.

### September 30

On September 30, programming will open to include:

- What Consumers Really Want, hosted by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy, senior smart home reviewer at The Verge, who will share what drives smart home purchase decisions, where consumers still encounter friction and which features matter most in everyday use.
- The Professional Installation Market, where new CEDIA research sets the stage for a conversation with professional integrators about changing customer expectations, common project challenges and new opportunities.
- Beyond the Single-Family Home, hosted by Jennifer Kent, SVP and Principal Analyst at Parks Associates, alongside leaders across multifamily, hospitality and PropTech to examine what it takes to deploy connected technology at scale and where commercial markets are creating new opportunities for Z-Wave.
- Preparing for the Next Wave of Cybersecurity Requirements, where experts examine the latest developments around Europe’s Cyber Resilience Act and the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark, what manufacturers need to do to prepare, and how Z-Wave’s architecture can help support compliance with both programs.

The day will conclude with an informal networking event that offers attendees the chance to continue discussions from the day, exchange ideas, and connect with colleagues from across the smart home and commercial IoT markets.

### October 1

The final day of Fall Summit will be dedicated to member-only Technical and Marketing Committee and Working Group sessions, giving Alliance members dedicated time to collaborate on ongoing initiatives and help shape priorities for the Z-Wave ecosystem.

#### Registration Details

Z-Wave Alliance members can register for the full Fall Summit for $699. Installers, integrators and non-members can register for $99. Non-Member registration includes access to the Z-Wave Feature Demo and opening reception on September 29 and the September 30 programming and networking event. Unplug Fest and the October 1 working sessions are exclusive to Z-Wave Alliance members.

The full agenda, registration and travel information are available on the [Z-Wave Fall Summit 2026 event page](https://z-wavealliance.org/eve/z-wave-fall-summit-2026/).

The A300L and A400U bring TCL’s art tv tech into a slim, flush-mountable design, with the A400U also incorporating TCL’s QD-Mini LEDs for greater picture quality.

Published: September 21, 2026Nick Boever

![TCL A300L Designer Series](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A300L_Lifestyle_2rs.jpg)

TCL A300L Designer Series. Images courtesy of TCL

Coming out [IFA](https://www.ifa-berlin.com/), TCL has expanded its flush-mounted Designer Series in the U.S. with two new lines, the A300L QLED and A400U QD-Mini LED Series. Both series will run on Google TV and include TCL’s Art Library, which offers users the option to display artwork at no subscription cost on the TV when not in use, allowing it to blend into the background. The TVs also include multiple matte options and a flush mount included in the box to help them better blend in with a home’s design.

## A300L Specs and Features

![TCL A300L Designer Series](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A300L_Lifestyle_People-scaled.jpg)

The A300L series comes in 55-, 65- and 75-inch models with an 85-inch model expected to arrive at an intermediate date. The 55- and 65-inch models measure 1.1 inches deep, allowing them to sit nearly flush against the wall. The 75- and 85-inch models still sport a slim profile, measuring 1.17 and 1.26 inches deep, respectively.

All models in the series come with an ultra-matte, anti-glare screen that is designed to reduce reflections while adhering to that canvas-like aesthetic. The series also come with off-white and light-wood magnetic frames that further help complete the look. Additional handcrafted options are also available through Laredo Factory Frames.

The screens themselves sport a 144 Hz refresh rate, according to TCL, with 4K UHD resolution that supports Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10 and HLG formats. It also comes with a built-in 20W stereo system with Dolby Atmos and Dolby Digital+ processing. There’s also 3.5mm connector options for external audio.

## A400U Specs and Features

![A400U TCL Designer Series](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A400U_Lifestyle_1-scaled.jpg)

The A400L series comes in 55-, 65-, 75-, 85- and 95-inch models with all models except the 95-inch sporting a screen depth of 1.6 inches. The 95-inch model comes in at 1.8 inches.

The A400U series keeps all the same art TV features of the A300L line with the main distinction being the QD-Mini LEDs, using TCL’s Halo Control System and Local Dimming Pro+ for improved backlight precision, contrast and blooming control.

The A400U also adds DTS:X spatial audio support.

#### Why Integrators Should Take Notice

The Designer Series is TCL’s follow-up to the NXTFRAME and NXTVISION TVs that originally marked TCL’s entry into the art TV category, now populated by the likes of Samsung, LG, SKYWORTH, Hisense, along with TCL.

While Samsung’s The Frame still stands as one of the gold-standards for lifestyle TVs in the custom integration (CI) channel, companies like SKYWORTH note the strong popularity of their own art TV offerings, highlighting the sheer popularity of the product category among integrators.

# WAC’s Spa-Ready TUCK Lights Arrive as More Connected Bath Solutions Enter the Channel

Already existing as outdoor luminaries, the TUCK, TUCK II and TUCK III have been updated with a heat-resistant model developed exclusively for saunas.

Published: September 17, 2026Nick Boever

![WAC Group Modern Forms TUCK sauna lights](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/WAC-GROUP-FMW256605-TUCK-SAUNA_V21-scaled.jpg)

Image courtesy of WAC Group

#### Key Takeaways

- The TUCK, TUCK II and TUCK III feature a heat-resistant model for saunas.
- All three models provide upwards of 600 lumens at 3000K CCT and 90 CRI.
- The update arrives as new connected bath and spa solutions enter channel.

* * *

WAC Group is releasing a new set of spa-grade lighting fixtures via its Modern Forms lineup. The TUCK series, which already exists as an outdoor luminary, has been updated for spas and saunas with added heat resistance to an already wet-rated design. According to WAC Group, “Spa and sauna lighting has been needed for quite some time,” with the updated TUCK fixtures looking to address that need.

The lights themselves come in three different iterations, yet all share a similar circular profile defined by a diffuser with banded ring design, which, when lit, emits a soft, even glow designed to provide ambient illumination starting at 600 max lumens.

While the outdoor version of the TUCK lights offers four different CCT colorways, the sauna option is only available in 3000K. It is, however, heat resistant up to 185 degrees Fahrenheit and sports a 90 CRI. Additionally, the lights can be mounted either on ceilings or wall in all orientations.

The Sauna-ready versions of TUCK, TUCK II, or TUCK III are also ADA-compliant, Title 24-compliant and ETL-listed.

#### Why integrators should take note

While the custom integration (CI) industry is no stranger to specialty spa and sauna installs in the home, the 2026 CEDIA Expo put a particularly strong spotlight on the category as companies like Kohler and Thermasol have started to explore the channel more with connected bath solutions.

On its own, this would merit nothing more a curious intrigue, but both brands received considerable interest from integrators at the show, highlighting the appetite this channel has for being able to provide a connected sauna or spa solution. For this reason, _CE Pro_ has [identified the connected bath and spa as being a potential breakout category for integrators](https://www.cepro.com/news/custom-integration-dreams-of-a-connected-bath-may-finally-be-here/628640/) in the coming years given both homeowner and integrator interest.

And like other design-driven, wellness-focused spaces, lighting will ultimately sit as one of the pillars of experience.

The Sauna-ready versions of TUCK, TUCK II, or TUCK III are also ADA-compliant, Title 24-compliant and ETL-listed.

While the custom integration (CI) industry is no stranger to specialty spa and sauna installs in the home, the 2026 CEDIA Expo put a particularly strong spotlight on the category as companies like Kohler and Thermasol have started to explore the channel more with connected bath solutions.

On its own, this would merit nothing more a curious intrigue, but both brands received considerable interest from integrators at the show, highlighting the appetite this channel has for being able to provide a connected sauna or spa solution. For this reason, CE Pro has identified the connected bath and spa as being a potential breakout category for integrators in the coming years given both homeowner and integrator interest.

And like other design-driven, wellness-focused spaces, lighting will ultimately sit as one of the pillars of experience.

# Devialet Unveils Pulse Blue Model for Phantom Ultimate Speaker

The new exclusive model revisits the brand’s original color identity while building upon the Phantom Ultimate’s audio architecture.

Published: September 17, 2026Nick Boever

![Devialet Phantom Ultimate Pulse Blue](https://www.cepro.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Devialet-Phantom-Ultimate_PulseBlue_KV_Product_1x1_Nuders.png)

Images courtesy of Devialet

#### Key Takeaways

- The Phantom Ultimate 98db – Pulse Blue revisits Devialet’s previously explored blue branding.
- The new Pulse Blue includes an extensive range of streaming protocols via AirPlay, Google Cast, Roon Ready, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, and UPnP.
- The new edition and its matching Tree stand are available for pre-order starting today across all Devialet stores, on Devialet.com, and through authorized retailers.

* * *

One year after introducing the latest generation of its iconic speaker (and a few weeks after announcing a version [built specifically for custom integration](https://www.cepro.com/news/devialet-returns-to-cedia-expo-in-2026-with-phantom-ultimate-custom/628062/)) Devialet has an all-new, limited edition marked by a new finish: the Phantom Ultimate 98 dB – Pulse Blue. The new look and model are part of a partnership the company has with Global Brand Ambassador Isack Hadjar, a Formula 1 driver for Oracle Red Bull Racing.

Pulse Blue revisits the brand’s previously explored color identity, shifting the finish of the speaker’s side panels from matte to gloss with a mirror-polished surface. A clear varnish further enhances the deep RAL 5011 blue, creating a vibrant, light-responsive finish. The logo has also been refined for total visual coherence.

The new speaker also comes with a new stand to complete the look.

## The Tech Behind the Phantom Ultimate Pulse Blue

The Devialet Phantom Ultimate 98 dB – Pulse Blue builds on the Devialet DOS 3 software architecture while also integrating an extensive range of streaming protocols via AirPlay, Google Cast, Roon Ready, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, and UPnP.

Beyond that, the Pulse Blue retains much of the original’s acoustic performance in a more compact form. The Pulse blue sports high-fidelity reproduction across frequency ranges from 18 Hz to 25 kHz (±6 dB), delivering up to 98 dB SPL.

An optimized audio chain supports files up to 24-bit / 192 kHz while a dedicated full-range driver broadens the acoustic field, to reproduce each note with precision and balance. Additionally, the Pulse Blue supports flexible listening in solo, stereo, or multi-room configurations, with compatibility across AirPlay, Google Cast, Roon Ready.

Through the Devialet app users can also access a 6-band equalizer to adjust frequencies as well as Bass Reducer and Loudness functionalities for added control over low-frequency intensity and improved acoustic compensation at lower volumes.

#### Price and Availability

The new edition and its matching Tree stand are available for pre-order starting today across all Devialet stores, on [Devialet.com](https://www.devialet.com/en-us/), and through authorized retailers, priced at $2,200 for the speaker and $349 for the Tree stand.
